sources.entry: Keylane - Source-available keyboard launcher for macOS 26+ with app and file search, clipboard history, and system actions.

summary.one_liner: Keylane is a native macOS keyboard launcher (opened with Option+Space) for searching apps, files, clipboard history, and running system actions, written in Swift and SwiftUI.
summary.what_it_does: Keylane opens a search window with Option+Space where you type an app, file, or command name, then navigate with arrow keys, open with Return, and dismiss with Escape. It searches applications (including pinyin and fuzzy matching, plus favorites), and files via Spotlight with a local supplementary index, directory and content search, and user-authorized folders. It keeps a clipboard history covering text, images, and files, with search, pinning, and retention settings. Utility tools include a calculator, Emoji and symbols, quick links, script commands, and text snippets. System integrations listed include Shortcuts, Calendar, Contacts, and screenshot search with OCR, and the README notes some of these still have unverified areas.
use_cases: launch macOS apps from the keyboard
search files and folders on a Mac
recover previously copied text, images, or files
run quick calculations or insert emoji and symbols
store and insert reusable text snippets
notable: Source-available with a GPL-3.0-or-later license on the current dev source; earlier Beta 1 and main snapshots carry PolyForm Noncommercial terms
Local-first design: no built-in telemetry or cloud sync; AI keys stored in macOS Keychain
Clipboard history with pinning and retention policies, plus optional persistence
Beta 1 is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so it requires manual installation
Repository includes isolated integration checks and a documented release workflow with Developer ID signing and notarization
caveats: Requires macOS 26+ and Apple Silicon; Intel and universal binaries are not yet verified
Beta 1 is ad-hoc signed, not notarized, and must be installed manually; macOS may block first launch
Several flows are still unverified per the README, including first launch, Navigation focus, multi-monitor, full screen, and Spaces; Raycast extension compatibility is in development and not shipped
Auto-paste and Finder selection features may require Accessibility or Automation permissions; file AI sends selected context to a configured service when the user submits
summary.license: GPL-3.0-or-later for current dev source (per README); Beta 1 and earlier snapshots under PolyForm Noncommercial
